gaps.note: an edit hides the transition to the lifetime sales question

stage_a.note: F1 maintains an energetic, engaging and positive tone throughout the pitch.
F1 shows strong excitement about the product's features and use cases.
F1 is friendly and approachable, smiling and engaging the panel.

venture.description: A wearable Bluetooth remote with large buttons to control smartphone music and calls without removing gloves.
venture.note: Seeking $250,000 in exchange for 8% of the company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 greets the panel, introduces himself and F2, and states their ask.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 playfully greets F2.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 also greets F2.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 greets F2.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 tries to get F2's attention, noting they are on national television.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 acts distracted by his earbuds and struggles to take them off with his ski gloves.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reacts to F2's struggle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains how the product solves the problem of controlling a phone with gloves on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 directs the panel's attention to the samples provided.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if the device connects to a phone via Bluetooth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms it does and asks S2 to put on gloves to try it.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 puts on the gloves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 instructs S2 to press the plus button to increase the volume.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 presses the button and the volume increases.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 encourages her to make it louder.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 continues testing the remote.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains other functions like playing music and answering calls.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 notes how easy it is to work and the difficulty of doing anything in a ski glove.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 shares the story of how they came up with the idea during a ski trip.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that they molded the idea into the current product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks how long the product has been on the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have been actively selling for three years.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what their lifetime sales are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the sales figures for the past two years.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks about the selling price and the cost to make the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details the landed cost and the retail price.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reacts positively to the retail price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 adds that they have 83 percent margins.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks what percentage of sales is spent on marketing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states their monthly marketing spend.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks for the customer acquisition cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the exact customer acquisition cost per unit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if skiing is the biggest application for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains it was initially for skiers but is now used by various other groups.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the product is waterproof.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies it is water-resistant and gives examples of its use.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 summarizes their economics and asks if they have taken money out of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 says no and mentions they have one investor.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how much the investor put in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the initial investment amount.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits, citing the risk of technical obsolescence from voice-automated products.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, feeling she cannot help the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, expressing concerns about the long-term survival against sophisticated earbuds.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, stating she is not tech-savvy enough to predict the market.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 offers the requested amount for slightly more equity and a high royalty until recouped.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 calculates their profit per unit to show the royalty is too high.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 argues it is not a lot of cash.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists they cannot do a ten-dollar royalty.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 suggests the founders make a counteroffer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters with a two-dollar royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks if they could even afford the proposed royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 complains it would take too long to get paid back at that rate.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains their current inventory and production plans to assure S2.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 insists on the ten-dollar royalty, calling it just a product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 warns S5 that his royalty will bankrupt the company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 argues their acquisition cost will drop, allowing them to afford the royalty.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 asks if S5 would accept a higher equity stake instead of a royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 refuses, stating he wants the royalty to align their incentives.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 questions why S5 wouldn't just take a percentage.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 dismisses S2's comment, noting she is not making an offer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 acknowledges S5's point about being the only one with an offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 tells them it is okay if they decline his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks if S5 would lower the royalty to three dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 refuses the three-dollar royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 states they are not selling enough units.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 argues they would sell more with S5's help.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 agrees but emphasizes he wants to be part of the business long-term.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: F2 counters with fifteen percent equity and a one-dollar royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 refuses the counteroffer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks the panel, implicitly rejecting the original offer and exiting.

decisions.note: Risk from voice automated products, not a fit.
Nothing she could help with, not for her.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 10% equity and a $10 per unit royalty until $1M is paid.
decisions.note: Likes the simple product, wants to get money back 3x.
Asks if Kevin would go down to $3 royalty.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 15% equity and a $1 per unit royalty until investment paid back.
decisions.note: Offers higher equity to lower the royalty.
Declines the offer after Kevin refuses the counter.

record.notes: The prepared presentation includes a short skit involving F2 pretending to listen to music with earbuds.
